acts.11.p1.b1.text: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

acts.11.p1.b2.text: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem,

acts.11.p1.b3.text: the circumcised believers took issue with him

acts.11.p1.b4.text: and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”

acts.11.p2.b1.text: But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:

acts.11.p2.b2.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.

acts.11.p2.b3.text: ‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’

acts.11.p2.b4.text: But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’

acts.11.p3.b1.text: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.

acts.11.p3.b2.text: These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.

acts.11.p3.b3.text: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.

acts.11.p3.b4.text: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’

acts.11.p4.b1.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.

acts.11.p4.b2.text: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’

acts.11.p4.b3.text: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ,

acts.11.p4.b4.text: who was I to hinder the work of God?”

acts.11.p5.b1.text: When they heard this, their objections were put to rest,

acts.11.p5.b3.text: “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”

acts.11.p6.b1.text: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch,

acts.11.p6.b2.text: speaking the message only to Jews.

acts.11.p6.b3.text: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.

acts.11.p6.b4.text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.

acts.11.p7.b1.text: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.

acts.11.p7.b2.text: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced

acts.11.p7.b3.text: and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.

acts.11.p7.b4.text: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.

acts.11.p8.b1.text: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,

acts.11.p8.b3.text: he brought him back to Antioch.

acts.11.p9.b1.text: So for a full year they met together with the church

acts.11.p9.b2.text: and taught large numbers of people.

acts.11.p9.b3.text: The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.

acts.11.p10.b1.text: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

acts.11.p10.b2.text: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world.

acts.11.p10.b3.text: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.

acts.11.p10.b4.text: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.
